audit.note: the 5 Avatars toast client-side via control_global MESSAGE_TOAST.show with '{0} Pressed' filled by $event.oSource.sId (roundtrip-free) - the app has no on_event

deviations.what: the sap.m.Avatar control (since UI5 1.73) is newer than 1.71 and is the whole point of this sample - kept 1:1, the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.73.

the Avatar properties badgeIcon and badgeTooltip (since UI5 1.77) and badgeValueState (since UI5 1.116) are what this sample demonstrates and are kept 1:1 - the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.116 to render the badge value states.

the icon sap-icon://information (in the icon font since UI5 1.80) is kept 1:1 as the badgeIcon of the 'Information' Avatar - below 1.80 the badge renders with no icon; covered by the >= 1.116 the badgeValueState already needs.

onInit's JSONModel (GettyImages/Shutterstock/LowShutterstock = sap.ui.require.toUrl('sap/m/images/...')) is seeded in model_init as the default-model root fields gettyimages and lowshutterstock - Shutterstock is never bound by this view, so it stays out of the model (unbound mock keys are not inlined). The module paths have no server-side resolution, so they are pinned to the OpenUI5 host https://sdk.openui5.org/test-resources/sap/m/images/ (same file names, the folder the sample's resourceRoots sap.m.images points at) per the runtime asset-URL rule. The bindings Avatar.src {/GettyImages} and {/LowShutterstock} stay bindings (client->_bind), which structural-diff cannot read statically.

onPress toasts oEvent.getSource().getId() + ' Pressed'. All 5 press wires reproduce that client-side and roundtrip-free (follow_up_action control_global MESSAGE_TOAST.show, template '{0} Pressed' filled by $event.oSource.sId, app 127 precedent); the id itself is a UI5 runtime value whose view prefix differs from the original's.
